previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and functional quadriplegia was admitted with fever, tachypnea, tachycardia, and hypotension. He was found to have a complicated urinary tract infection caused by Providencia rettgeri and hospital-associated pneumonia with pulmonary edema. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics initially, then narrowed to cefepime based on culture results. His sepsis resolved, hypotension improved with fluids and brief pressor support, and hypernatremia corrected with free water. Renal function returned to baseline. He was discharged to extended care on day 5 to complete a 10-day course of IV cefepime, with follow-up planned for pulmonary and infectious disease.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History: ___ with ams, pna// pna

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___ for mastoid institution.

FINDINGS: 

Tracheostomy terminates midline approximately 5 cm above the carina.  Lung
volumes are low, unchanged.  Diffuse airspace and interstitial opacities have
worsened since prior examination.  Cardiac silhouette is predominately
obscured but likely normal in size. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion
appreciated. Enteric tube overlies the upper abdomen.

IMPRESSION: 

Multifocal pneumonia superimposed on chronic lung disease.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with altered mental status, AIDS.  Evaluate for
enhancing lesions, hemorrhage.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images from skullbase to vertex were obtained
without intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations and bone
algorithms reconstructions were also performed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Sequenced Acquisition 16.0 s, 16.0 cm; CTDIvol = 50.2 mGy (Head) DLP =
802.7 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is no intracranial hemorrhage.  Ill-defined slightly hyperdense region
in the left insula and basal ganglia causes mass effect on ventricle which is
asymmetrically smaller right (02:16, 601b:49).  Periventricular and bibasilar
calcifications are present, left temporal.  Global atrophy is noted. 
Periventricular white hypodensities are nonspecific. Right frontal lobe
encephalomalacia near the vertex noted.  The ventricles and sulci are
prominent consistent with involutional changes.  There is minimal if any
midline shift.

No acute osseous abnormalities seen.  Chronic postsurgical changes in the
right frontal calvarium.  There is partial opacification of the ethmoid
sinuses and mucosal thickening in both maxillary sinuses.  The mastoid air
cells, and middle ear cavities are clear. The orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. Ill-defined left basal ganglia and insular soft tissue prominence causes
mass effect on the left lateral ventricle and could represent a mass.  MRI
with contrast is recommended for further characterization.
2. No intracranial hemorrhage.
COMMENTS ON ATTENDING REVIEW:
There is no mass effect.  While both ventricles are enlarged due to global
parenchymal volume loss, as are the cerebral sulci, there is asymmetric ex
vacuo enlargement of the right lateral ventricle due to a chronic infarct
involving the right caudate, lentiform nucleus, right internal capsule, and
right corona radiata, as well as due to the right frontal cortical
encephalomalacia which may be secondary to infarct, prior trauma, or prior
surgery given the overlying right frontal burr hole.

There are multifocal calcifications in the periventricular regions, basal
ganglia, and posterior left temporal lobe, with adjacent left temporal
encephalomalacia/gliosis.  These are suggestive of prior intracranial
infection, particularly in the setting of AIDS.

Confluent supratentorial white matter hypodensities are nonspecific and may
reflect a combination of postinfectious/postinflammatory changes, AIDS
dementia, and chronic small vessel ischemic changes.

There is moderate opacification of bilateral anterior ethmoid air cells which
appears to be secondary to mucosal thickening.  There is mild mucosal
thickening and aerosolized secretions in bilateral posterior ethmoid air
cells.  Left sphenoid sinus is almost completely opacified.  There is mild
mucosal thickening in the right sphenoid sinus.  There is moderate right and
mild left maxillary sinus mucosal thickening with polypoid components in the
right maxillary sinus.  There is trace opacification of left mastoid tip air
cells.

ATTENDING IMPRESSION:


No clear evidence for acute intracranial abnormalities on noncontrast CT. 
However, MRI would be more sensitive for active infection or mass, if
clinically warranted.
